title: inspection-findings
description: The envelope one inspection of one scope writes. It is a file the agent wrote rather than anything parsed out of what it printed: a format enforced by nothing breaks silently, and a malformed finding read out of prose would be indistinguishable from no finding at all. ITS ITEMS ARE TYPED AS OBJECTS AND NOTHING MORE, and that is deliberate rather than lax. This validator subset has no reference keyword, so restating the brief's fields here would be a second definition of a shape this repository defines once in schemas/story-brief.schema.json — two definitions that agree today and drift the first time either is edited. Each finding is instead held to the brief schema on its own, which is also what makes one malformed finding cost only itself: it is dropped and named with the field that failed, and the findings beside it in the same file are filed exactly as they would have been.

findings.description: The findings this inspection of this scope produced, each of which is separately held to schemas/story-brief.schema.json. An empty array is an answer rather than an absence: it says the Inspector looked at this scope and found nothing worth filing.

area_suggestions.description: What the Inspector could name no area for, and what it thinks each such brief concerns. Optional: an envelope carrying only `findings` is what every inspection wrote before this existed and is what an inspection of a target declaring no area vocabulary goes on writing. Each item names by slug the brief it is about, so a suggestion for a finding that was dropped rather than filed is matched to nothing and is not printed. IT IS READ FOR THE REPORT AND FILED BY NOTHING: a suggestion never reaches a brief, a payload, an outbox entry or a tracker, because the vocabulary grows by a person editing the target's own document and a name no developer has approved must not be filed under. What it buys is that a missing area is reported rather than silent, which is the whole reason naming none is a first-class answer.

slug.description: The slug of the finding this suggestion is about, spelled exactly as that finding spells it. It is how a report matches a suggestion to a brief that was actually filed.

concerns.description: What that brief seems to concern, in the Inspector's own words, so a person can decide whether the target's vocabulary is missing a line. It is not a name being proposed for the vocabulary and nothing files it.
